 By  
 Hannah Postlethwait 
 Published Oct 28, 2026, 6:24 AM EDT 
 Hannah Postlethwait is an author and entertainment journalist living in Iowa. A lifelong writer, Hannah refined her skills at Iowa State University, graduating with degrees in journalism and American Indian Studies, catalyzing her passion for fair and accurate diversity representation in mass media.
Hannah wrote her debut novel after graduating, completing a work of speculative fiction that explores the future of AI integration and its ingraining effects on the human experience. During that time, Hannah worked in commerce, healthcare, and marketing to deepen her understanding of the human condition and the marketplace.
After completing her book, Hannah was eager to return to journalism and features writing, securing a position at ScreenRant that led to her role at CBR. A senior writer for the site, Hannah discusses the latest in television and streaming, specializing in the network TV cycle.
Hannah is drawn to the complexities of formatting a television narrative and is fascinated by the successes and failures in the industry. Her current work expands her understanding of what makes a series memorable, research she uses to craft her own stories.

 ABC has confirmed that High Potential fans will have to wait considerably longer than usual for Season 3. Despite renewing its entire scripted lineup for the 2026–2027 broadcast season, the network left one of its biggest hits off the fall schedule, pushing Kaitlin Olson’s procedural into 2027 and creating the longest hiatus in the show’s history.

 The delay is especially notable considering High Potential ’s performance. The series finished the 2025–2026 season with 16.01 million viewers over 35 days across ABC and streaming, ranking as the No. 1 broadcast entertainment series among adults 18-49 and No. 3 in total viewers. Yet unlike its first two seasons, Season 3 will not air a single new episode in 2026.
 ABC’s 2026-2027 TV Lineup Marks a Major Shift
 ABC’s fall 2026 schedule is now well underway, with returning favorites including Abbott Elementary, 9-1-1, 9-1-1: Nashville, and Grey’s Anatomy. However, the network deliberately held several established shows and new projects until 2027 rather than crowding them into the fall schedule.
 ABC has also launched comedy-drama R.J. Decker, starring Scott Speedman as the title character. Per the official synopsis, “R.J. Decker is a disgraced newspaper photographer and ex-con who starts over as a private investigator in the colorful-if-crime-filled world of South Florida.” The series currently airs Tuesdays at 10 p.m. on ABC.
 The network’s fall lineup also includes the revived Scrubs , along with unscripted staples such as Dancing with the Stars, Shark Tank, Celebrity Wheel of Fortune, and America’s Funniest Home Videos. That gives ABC a full schedule even without several of its established scripted performers returning before the end of 2026.
 Viewers will notice that some of ABC's most outstanding TV shows are still absent from the fall lineup. The Rookie is again being held for midseason, while its new spinoff, The Rookie: North, will also debut in 2027. Shifting Gears and High Potential are likewise being saved for later in the broadcast season.
 High Potential Season 3 Still Faces Its Longest Hiatus Yet
 Kaitlin Olson as Morgan and Daniel Sunjata as Karadec at the police station in High Potential 'The One That Got Away' Image via ABC 
 ABC’s decision to hold back one of its most popular scripted series creates the longest break High Potential has faced between seasons. Seasons 1 and 2 both occupied prominent places on the network’s fall schedule, while Season 3 will not begin until 2027 as part of ABC’s midseason programming.
 The U.S. version of High Potential stars It’s Always Sunny in Philadelphia ’s Kaitlin Olson as Morgan Gillory, a mother of three who receives a job offer from the LAPD Major Crimes Division after solving a case while working her night shift as a cleaner. Olson’s performance quickly helped distinguish the series from ABC’s other procedurals.
 ABC moved High Potential out of the fall lineup as part of a broader scheduling strategy intended to give the show a more consistent run with fewer interruptions. Still, ABC dropping High Potential ’s formula in 2026 means fans will go considerably longer without new episodes than they did between the show’s first two seasons.
 The network has since confirmed that a new episode of High Potential will air immediately after Super Bowl LXI on Feb. 14, 2027, giving Season 3 a major promotional boost when it returns. New episodes will also air on Tuesdays, although ABC still has not announced the exact Season 3 premiere date.
 That high-profile return does not erase the downside of the scheduling change. High Potential Season 1 consisted of 13 episodes, while Season 2 expanded to 18, and ABC has not yet announced how many episodes Season 3 will contain. Fans are therefore facing both the show’s longest hiatus and some uncertainty about the size of its next season.
 The delay stands out even more because of how successful High Potential has been. The procedural finished last season as the No. 1 broadcast entertainment series among adults 18-49 and No. 3 in total viewers, making it unusual for one of ABC’s strongest performers to sit out the entire fall portion of the broadcast season.

 Other networks are making similar changes with established hits. For instance, CBS ends an era for Ghosts , moving its supernatural sitcom to its midseason lineup for the first time in the show’s run. In High Potential ’s case, ABC is clearly planning a major return, but fans still have to endure a substantially longer wait before Morgan is back on screen.
